newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES BEAT PENGUINS 3-1.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES BEAT PENGUINS 3-1.

text.p: Dominik Hasek turned aside 21 shots for his league-leading 25th victory and Rob Ray and Mike Peca scored first-period goals, helping the Buffalo Sabres to a 3-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Richard Smehlik added an empty-net goal for the Sabres, who won for the fifth time in seven games.
Jaromir Jagr scored the lone goal for the Penguins.

"That hard work thing kind of slipped way from us a litle, we were staying away from our game plan," Ray said. "Tonight we concentrated the last couple of days in practice, we have been working on it."
At Colorado, Scott Young and Claude Lemieux each scored twice and Patrick Roy made a successful return to the lineup as the Colorado Avalanche blitzed the slumping Los Angeles Kings, 6-3.
Mike Ricci added a goal and an assist, helping the Avalanche, which took control with a four-goal first period, extend their home unbeaten streak to six games.

In Dallas, Joe Nieuwendyk and Mike Modano scored power-play goals and Andy Moog made 25 saves, helping the Dallas Stars extend their unbeaten streak to five games with a 3-1 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
Sergei Zubov added a goal and an assist for Dallas, which is 4-0-1 in its last five to open a nine-point lead over second-place Detroit in the Central Division.
In Detroit, Nikolai Khabibulin made 30 saves for his second shutout in five days and Keith Tkachuk had a goal and assist to lead the Phoenix Coyotes to a 3-0 victory over the Detroit Red Wings.
Khabibulin stopped seven shots in the first period, 14 in the second and nine in the third as he improved to 14-21-3.

In Edmonton, Curtis Joseph made 34 saves, including all 18 over the final two periods, and Andrei Kovalenko's goal late in the second period snapped a tie, lifting the Edmonton Oilers to their third straight victory, 3-1 over the San Jose Sharks.
Joseph allowed Shean Donovan's fourth goal of the season 2:51 into the game, but kept San Jose scoreless thereafter. Joseph has won his last three starts, giving up one goal in each.
"We didn't give them a ton of glorious chances even though they had a lot of shots," Joseph said. "We weren't exactly flying tonight but we were still good enough to win."
At New Jersey, rookie Jay Pandolfo's goal with 10:25 left in regulation lifted the New Jersey Devils into a 1-1 tie with the Ottawa Senators in a battle of two of the NHL's lowest-scoring teams.

The Devils were trailing 1-0 when Pandolfo grabbed a loose puck along the right boards after a faceoff. He backhanded a pass into the corner to Bobby Holik, who threw it in front. Pandolfo flicked a short wrist shot past goaltender Damian Rhodes for his third goal of the season.

In Toronto, Grant Fuhr made 29 saves for his second shutout of the season and Pierre Turgeon and Brett Hull had a goal and an assist apiece as the surging St. Louis Blues blanked the Toronto Maple Leafs 4-0.
Fuhr, a former Maple Leaf, was hardly tested in recording his 19th career shutout and fifth with the Blues. He stopped seven shots in the first and 11 in both the second and third periods.

Al MacInnis and Joe Murphy also scored for St. Louis.

In Washington, Ron Hextall made 29 saves and Dainius Zubrus' power-play goal midway through the second period proved to be the game-winner as the Philadelphia Flyers edged the Washington Capitals 2-1.
Hextall faced only six shots in the third period, but came up with a trio of big saves over the first two. Rod Brind'Amour also scored for the Flyers.
Brind'Amour staked Philadelphia to a 1-0 lead in the first period.
